resume: Finding a leisure center for Wednesdays and school holidays, the file to prepare (up-to-date vaccinations, family quotient) and support from the Caf de la Guadeloupe.
aQuoiCaSert: Non-residential leisure centers (ALSH, accueils de loisirs sans hébergement, often called centres de loisirs) take children from the time they start school up to adolescence, including children with disabilities. Depending on the town, they operate on Wednesdays, before or after school, at lunchtime and during school holidays. Each organizer sets its own prices, often based on household income and taking into account support from the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office).
quiEstConcerne: Parents of school-age children looking for care on Wednesdays or during the holidays.
Low-income families receiving Caf benefits, for the Caf's holiday and free-time support.
aSavoir: Places are limited: find out several weeks before the holidays or the start of the school year. You usually register with the town hall (mairie) or the center itself.
Mandatory vaccinations are required for admission to group settings, including after-school care and holiday camps. The list, the same as in mainland France, depends on the child's year of birth.
If vaccinations are not up to date, a provisional 3-month admission is possible while they are done. The health record book (carnet de santé), filled in by the doctor, serves as proof.
Holiday and free-time support comes under each Caf's own social action program: amount and conditions vary from one department to another.

Separated parents: each parent can register the child for their own holiday weeks. Tell the center who is authorized to pick up the child and, if needed, provide the decision setting the child's residence.
